questions.question_text: Which formula gives the surface area of an **open** hemisphere (a bowl with no flat face) of radius $r$?

options.why: This is the closed hemisphere, which also counts the flat circular face.
This is the surface area of a whole sphere, not a half.
This is only the flat circular face, not the curved surface.

questions.solution_text:
An open hemisphere is half a sphere's curved surface: $\frac{1}{2} \times 4\pi r^{2} = 2\pi r^{2}$, with no flat face.
$A = 2\pi r^{2}$

questions.question_text: A closed hemisphere and an open hemisphere both have a radius of $4$ cm. How much greater is the closed hemisphere's surface area? Give an exact answer in terms of $\pi$.

options.why: Used the whole curved surface $2\pi r^{2}$ as the difference instead of the flat circle.
Halved the flat circle $\pi r^{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
Closed: $3\pi r^{2}$
Open: $2\pi r^{2}$
Difference $= \pi r^{2}$
$= \pi(4)^{2}$
$= 16\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
